sam (Customer): Hey team — hitting a 400 from /v1/rerank. Error message is 'invalid candidate format'. Our frontend sends candidates from the browser. Posting a quick curl that reproduces what we send (we think):

sam (Customer): ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' \
  -d '{"query": "Which is better?", "candidates": "[{\"id\":\"1\",\"text\":\"A\"}]", "top_k": 1}'
```

sam (Customer): The server responds with:

sam (Customer): ```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"type":"invalid_request","message":"candidates must be an array of objects"},"request_id":"req_ABC123"}
```

maria (Support): Thanks — can you paste the raw request payload (as seen by the server) or the SDK code you use? Also what's the exact Content-Type header that hits our gateway?

sam (Customer): I grabbed the raw body from our gateway logs. Looks like candidates arrives as a string and there's a BOM at the start: `\ufeff[{"id":"1","text":"A"}]` (so bytes EF BB BF before the bracket). Also in our front-end we were using FormData if the JSON body was built from a file upload — possible culprit.

devon (Engineer): That BOM + FormData combo explains it. If the client sends multipart/form-data or urlencoded rather than application/json, our parser sees candidates as a string. The BOM can cause the server-side JSON parser to fail to coerce the string into an array.

devon (Engineer): Quick repro that fails (mimics the FormData path):

devon (Engineer): ```
# this uses form field, so candidates is a string on the server side
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' \
  -F 'query=Which is better?' \
  -F 'candidates=@candidates.json;type=application/json'
# candidates.json contains a leading BOM in some builds
```

maria (Support): Workaround — send application/json body explicitly or ensure the file content is stripped of BOM. Example good request:

maria (Support): ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"Which is better?","candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"A"}],"top_k":1}'
```

maria (Support): Also, if you use the JS SDK, please try v2.3.0 — v2.2.1 had a bug where uploading from a File/Blob could switch the request to multipart and include BOM bytes. We're rolling a patch note, but for now explicit JSON header or stripping BOM fixes it.

opsbot (Infra-bot): Logged request req_ABC123 -> route: /v1/rerank -> gateway parsed body as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, candidates string length 37 (starts with BOM)

sam (Customer): Tried the explicit Content-Type approach and it worked — 200 and results returned. Thanks! :thumbsup:

maria (Support): Great, marking as resolved. If you want, send the original candidates.json file and we can run a quick script to strip BOM automatically before upload.
